stem: Verify that \(y \sec x = \tan x + c\) is a solution of the differential equation \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y \tan x = \sec x\).
solution: Here \(y \sec x = \tan x + c\). Differentiate w. r. t. x, we get \(y \sec x \tan x + \sec x \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \sec^2 x\). Therefore \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y \tan x = \sec x\). Hence \(y \sec x = \tan x + c\) is a solution of the differential equation \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y \tan x = \sec x\).

stem: Verify that \(y = \log x + c\) is a solution of the differential equation \(x \dfrac{d^2 y}{dx^2} + \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\).
solution: Here \(y = \log x + c\). Differentiate w. r. t. x, we get \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{x}\). Therefore \(x \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1\). Differentiate w. r. t. x, we get \(x \dfrac{d^2 y}{dx^2} + \dfrac{dy}{dx} \times 1 = 0\). Therefore \(x \dfrac{d^2 y}{dx^2} + \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\). \(y = \log x + c\) is the solution of \(x \dfrac{d^2 y}{dx^2} + \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\).

stem: Find the general solution of the differential equation \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x \sqrt{25 - x^2}\).
solution: \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x \sqrt{25 - x^2}\). Therefore \(dy = x \sqrt{25 - x^2} \cdot dx\). Integrating both sides, we get \(\int dy = \int \sqrt{25 - x^2} \cdot x \cdot dx\) ... (I). Put \(25 - x^2 = t\). Therefore \(-2x \cdot dx = dt\). Therefore \(x \cdot dx = -\dfrac{dt}{2}\). Eq. (I) becomes, \(\int dy = \int \sqrt{t}\left(-\dfrac{dt}{2}\right)\). Therefore \(2 \int dy = -\int \sqrt{t} \cdot dt\). Therefore \(2 \int dy + \int t^{\frac{1}{2}} \cdot dt = 0\). Therefore \(2y + \dfrac{t^{\frac{3}{2}}}{\frac{3}{2}} = c_1\). Therefore \(2y + \dfrac{2}{3} t^{\frac{3}{2}} = c_1\). Therefore \(6y + 2 t^{\frac{3}{2}} = 3 c_1\). Therefore \(6y + 2 (25 - x^2)^{\frac{3}{2}} = c\), where \(c = 3 c_1\).

stem: Find the general solution of the differential equation \(\dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{x \log x}{t}\).
solution: \(\dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{x \log x}{t}\). Therefore \(\dfrac{dx}{x \log x} = \dfrac{dt}{t}\). Integrating both sides, we get \(\int \dfrac{dx}{x \log x} = \int \dfrac{dt}{t}\). Therefore \(\log(\log x) = \log(t) + \log c\). Therefore \(\log(\log x) = \log(tc)\). Therefore \(\log x = ct\). Therefore \(e^{ct} = x\).

stem: Find the particular solution with given initial conditions: \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{2y} \cos x\) when \(x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\), \(y = 0\).
solution: \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{2y} \cos x\). Therefore \(\dfrac{dy}{e^{2y}} = \cos x \cdot dx\). Therefore \(e^{-2y} \cdot dy = \cos x \cdot dx\). Integrating both sides, we get \(\int e^{-2y} \cdot dy = \int \cos x \cdot dx\). Therefore \(\dfrac{e^{-2y}}{-2} = \sin x + c\) ... (I). When \(x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\), \(y = 0\). So eq. (I) becomes \(\dfrac{e^0}{-2} = \sin \dfrac{\pi}{6} + c\). Therefore \(-\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} + c\). Therefore \(-\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2} = c\), therefore \(c = -1\). Put in eq. (I), we get \(\dfrac{e^{-2y}}{-2} = \sin x - 1\). Therefore \(-e^{-2y} = 2\sin x - 2\). Therefore \(e^{2y}(2\sin x - 2) + 1 = 0\) is the required particular solution.

stem: Find the particular solution with given initial conditions: \(\dfrac{y - 1}{y + 1} + \dfrac{x - 1}{x + 1} \cdot \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\), when \(x = y = 2\).
solution: \(\dfrac{y - 1}{y + 1} + \dfrac{x - 1}{x + 1} \cdot \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\). Therefore \(\dfrac{x + 1}{x - 1} \cdot dx + \dfrac{y + 1}{y - 1} \cdot dy = 0\). Therefore \(\dfrac{(x - 1) + 2}{x - 1} \cdot dx + \dfrac{(y - 1) + 2}{y - 1} \cdot dy = 0\). Therefore \(\left(1 + \dfrac{2}{x - 1}\right) \cdot dx + \left(1 + \dfrac{2}{y - 1}\right) \cdot dy = 0\). Integrating, we get \(\int dx + 2 \int \dfrac{dx}{x - 1} + \int dy + 2 \int \dfrac{dy}{y - 1} = 0\). Therefore \(x + 2 \log(x - 1) + y + 2 \log(y - 1) = c\). Therefore \(x + y + 2 \log[(x - 1)(y - 1)] = c\) ... (I). When \(x = 2\), \(y = 2\). So eq. (I) becomes \(2 + 2 + 2 \log[(2 - 1)(2 - 1)] = c\). Therefore \(4 + 2 \log(1 \times 1) = c\). Therefore \(4 + 2 \log 1 = c\). Therefore \(4 + 2(0) = c\). Therefore \(c = 4\). Put in eq. (I), we get \(x + y + 2 \log[(x - 1)(y - 1)] = 4\) is required particular solution.

stem: Reduce the following differential equation to the separated variable form and hence find the general solution: \(1 + \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \operatorname{cosec}(x + y)\).
solution: \(1 + \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \operatorname{cosec}(x + y)\) ... (I). Put \(x + y = u\). Therefore \(1 + \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{du}{dx}\). Given differential equation becomes \(\dfrac{du}{dx} = \operatorname{cosec} u\). Therefore \(\dfrac{du}{\operatorname{cosec} u} = dx\). Therefore \(\sin u \cdot du = dx\). Integrating both sides, we get \(\int \sin u \cdot du = \int dx\). Therefore \(-\cos u = x + c\). Therefore \(x + \cos u + c = 0\). Therefore \(x + \cos(x + y) + c = 0\) (since \(x + y = u\)).

stem: Reduce the following differential equation to the separated variable form and hence find the general solution: \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = (4x + y + 1)^2\).
solution: \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = (4x + y + 1)^2\) ... (I). Put \(4x + y + 1 = u\). Therefore \(4 + \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{du}{dx}\). Therefore \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{du}{dx} - 4\). Given differential equation becomes \(\dfrac{du}{dx} - 4 = u^2\). Therefore \(\dfrac{du}{dx} = u^2 + 4\). Therefore \(\dfrac{du}{u^2 + 4} = dx\). Integrating both sides, we get \(\int \dfrac{du}{u^2 + 4} = \int dx\). Therefore \(\dfrac{1}{2} \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{u}{2}\right) = x + c_1\). Therefore \(\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{u}{2}\right) = 2x + 2c_1\). Therefore \(\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{4x + y + 1}{2}\right) = 2x + c\), where \(2c_1 = c\).

stem: Solve the differential equation \(x^2 y \cdot dx - (x^3 + y^3) \cdot dy = 0\).
solution: \(x^2 y \cdot dx - (x^3 + y^3) \cdot dy = 0\). Therefore \(x^2 y - (x^3 + y^3) \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\) ... (I). This is homogeneous Differential equation. Put \(y = vx\) ... (II). Differentiate w. r. t. x, we get \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x \dfrac{dv}{dx}\) ... (III). Put (II) and (III) in Eq. (I), it becomes, \(x^2 \cdot vx - (x^3 + v^3 x^3)\left(v + x \dfrac{dv}{dx}\right) = 0\). Divide by \(x^3\), we get \(v - (1 + v^3)\left(v + x \dfrac{dv}{dx}\right) = 0\). Therefore \(v - v - x \dfrac{dv}{dx} - v^4 - v^3 x \dfrac{dv}{dx} = 0\). Therefore \(-x(1 + v^3) \dfrac{dv}{dx} = v^4\). Therefore \(\dfrac{1 + v^3}{v^4} \cdot dv = -\dfrac{dx}{x}\). Therefore \(\left(\dfrac{1}{v^4} - \dfrac{v^3}{v^4}\right) dv + \dfrac{dx}{x} = 0\). Integrating eq., we get \(\int v^{-4} dv + \int \dfrac{dv}{v} + \int \dfrac{dx}{x} = c_1\). Therefore \(\dfrac{v^{-3}}{-3} + \log(v) + \log(x) = c_1\). Therefore \(\log(vx) = c_1 + \dfrac{v^{-3}}{3}\), therefore \(\log(y) = c_1 + \dfrac{1}{3} \cdot \dfrac{v^{-3}}{x^{-3}}\). Therefore \(3 \log(y) = 3 c_1 + \dfrac{x^3}{y^3}\). Therefore \(3 \log y = \dfrac{x^3}{y^3} + c\), where \(c = 3 c_1\).

stem: Solve the differential equation \(x \dfrac{dy}{dx} = x \tan\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) + y\).
solution: \(x \dfrac{dy}{dx} = x \tan\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) + y\) ... (I). This is homogeneous Differential equation. Put \(y = vx\) ... (II). Differentiate w. r. t. x, we get \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x \dfrac{dv}{dx}\) ... (III). Put (II) and (III) in Eq. (I), it becomes, \(x\left(v + x \dfrac{dv}{dx}\right) = x \tan\left(\dfrac{vx}{x}\right) + vx\). Divide by x, we get \(v + x \dfrac{dv}{dx} = \tan v + v\). Therefore \(x \dfrac{dv}{dx} = \tan v\). Therefore \(\dfrac{dv}{\tan v} = \dfrac{dx}{x}\). Integrating eq., we get \(\int \cot v \, dv = \int \dfrac{dx}{x}\). Therefore \(\log(\sin v) = \log(x) + \log c\). Therefore \(\log(\sin v) = \log(x \times c)\). Therefore \(\sin v = cx\). Therefore \(\sin\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) = cx\) is the solution.

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y + \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}}{x}\) ... (I). It is homogeneous differential equation. Put \(y = vx\) ... (II). Differentiate w. r. t. x, we get \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x \dfrac{dv}{dx}\) ... (III). Put (II) and (III) in Eq. (I), it becomes, \(v + x \dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{vx + \sqrt{x^2 + v^2 x^2}}{x}\). Therefore \(v + x \dfrac{dv}{dx} = v + \sqrt{1 + v^2}\). Therefore \(x \dfrac{dv}{dx} = \sqrt{1 + v^2}\). Therefore \(\dfrac{dv}{\sqrt{1 + v^2}} = \dfrac{dx}{x}\) ... (IV). Integrating eq. (IV), we get \(\int \dfrac{dv}{\sqrt{1 + v^2}} = \int \dfrac{dx}{x}\). Therefore \(\log(v + \sqrt{1 + v^2}) = \log(x) + \log c\). Therefore \(\log(v + \sqrt{1 + v^2}) = \log(cx)\). Therefore \(v + \sqrt{1 + v^2} = cx\). Therefore \(\dfrac{y}{x} + \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{y^2}{x^2}} = cx\). Therefore \(y + \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} = cx^2\) is the solution.

stem: Solve the differential equation \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = e^{-x}\).
solution: \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = e^{-x}\) ... (I). This is linear differential equation of the form \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q\) where \(P = 1\), \(Q = e^{-x}\). It's Solution is \(y \, (\text{I.F.}) = \int Q \cdot (\text{I.F.}) \, dx + c\) ... (II) where I.F. \(= e^{\int P dx} = e^{\int dx} = e^x\). eq. (II) becomes, \(y \cdot e^x = \int e^{-x} \times e^x \cdot dx + c\). Therefore \(y \cdot e^x = \int e^{-x + x} \cdot dx + c\). Therefore \(y \cdot e^x = \int e^0 \cdot dx + c\). Therefore \(y \cdot e^x = \int dx + c\). Therefore \(y \cdot e^x = x + c\) is the general solution.

stem: Solve the differential equation \(x \sin x \dfrac{dy}{dx} + (x \cos x + \sin x) y = \sin x\).
solution: \(x \sin x \dfrac{dy}{dx} + (x \cos x + \sin x) y = \sin x\). Divide by \(x \sin x\), we get \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(\cot x + \dfrac{1}{x}\right) y = \dfrac{1}{x}\) ... (I). It is the linear differential equation of the type \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q\) where \(P = \cot x + \dfrac{1}{x}\), \(Q = \dfrac{1}{x}\). Its solution is \(y \, (\text{I.F.}) = \int Q \cdot (\text{I.F.}) \, dx + c\) ... (II) where I.F. \(= e^{\int P dx} = e^{\int \left(\cot x + \frac{1}{x}\right) dx} = e^{\int \cot x \, dx + \int \frac{dx}{x}} = e^{\log|\sin x| + \log x} = x \sin x\). eq. (II) becomes, \(y \cdot x \sin x = \int \dfrac{1}{x} \times x \sin x \cdot dx + c\). Therefore \(xy \cdot \sin x = -\cos x + c\). Therefore \(xy \cdot \sin x + \cos x = c\) is the general solution.

stem: Solve the differential equation \((1 + y^2) dx = (\tan^{-1} y - x) dy\).
solution: \((1 + y^2) dx = (\tan^{-1} y - x) dy\). Therefore \(\dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{(\tan^{-1} y - x)}{(1 + y^2)}\). Therefore \(\dfrac{dx}{dy} + \left(\dfrac{1}{1 + y^2}\right) x = \dfrac{\tan^{-1} y}{1 + y^2}\). This is linear differential equation of the type \(\dfrac{dx}{dy} + Px = Q\) where \(P = \dfrac{1}{1 + y^2}\), \(Q = \dfrac{\tan^{-1} y}{1 + y^2}\). Its solution is \(x \, (\text{I.F.}) = \int Q \cdot (\text{I.F.}) \, dy + c\) ... (II) where I.F. \(= e^{\int P dy} = e^{\int \frac{1}{1 + y^2} dy} = e^{\tan^{-1} y}\). eq. (II) becomes, \(x \cdot e^{\tan^{-1} y} = \int \dfrac{\tan^{-1} y}{1 + y^2} \cdot e^{\tan^{-1} y} \, dy + c\) ... (III). in R.H.S. Put \(\tan^{-1} y = t\), differentiate w. r. t. x, we get \(\dfrac{dy}{1 + y^2} = dt\). eq. (III) becomes \(x \cdot e^{\tan^{-1} y} = \int t \cdot e^t \, dt + c = t \int e^t \cdot dt - \int [1 \times e^t] \, dt + c = t \cdot e^t - \int e^t \, dt + c = t \cdot e^t - e^t + c\). Therefore \(x \cdot e^{\tan^{-1} y} = \tan^{-1} y \cdot e^{\tan^{-1} y} - e^{\tan^{-1} y} + c\). Therefore \(x = \tan^{-1} y - 1 + \dfrac{c}{e^{\tan^{-1} y}}\). Therefore \(x + 1 - \tan^{-1} y = c \cdot e^{-\tan^{-1} y}\) is the solution.

stem: The slope of the tangent to the curve at any point is equal to \(y + 2x\). Find the equation of the curve passing through the origin.
solution: Let \(P(x, y)\) be any point on the curve \(y = f(x)\). The slope of the tangent at point \(P(x, y)\) is \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\). Therefore \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y + 2x\). Therefore \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} - y = 2x\). This is linear differential equation of the type \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q\) where \(P = -1\), \(Q = 2x\). Its solution is \(y \, (\text{I.F.}) = \int Q \cdot (\text{I.F.}) \, dx + c\) ... (I) where I.F. \(= e^{\int P dx} = e^{\int -dx} = e^{-x}\). eq. (I) becomes, \(y \cdot e^{-x} = \int 2x \times e^{-x} \, dx + c\). Therefore \(y \cdot e^{-x} = 2 \int x e^{-x} \, dx + c\) ... (II). Consider, \(\int x e^{-x} \, dx = x \int e^{-x} \, dx - \int \left(1 \times \dfrac{e^{-x}}{-1}\right) dx = \dfrac{x e^{-x}}{-1} + \int e^{-x} \, dx = -x e^{-x} + \int e^{-x} \, dx = -x e^{-x} - e^{-x} + c\). (II) becomes \(y \cdot e^{-x} = 2[-x e^{-x} - e^{-x}] + c\). Therefore \(y = -2x - 2 + c e^{-x}\) ... (III). The curve passes through the origin \((0, 0)\). Therefore \(0 = -2(0) - 2 + c e^0\). Therefore \(0 = -2 + c\). Therefore \(2 = c\). Put in (III). Therefore \(y = -2x - 2 + 2 e^{-x}\). Therefore \(2x + y + 2 = 2 e^{-x}\) is the equation of the curve.
